name: Konrad Zuse School of Excellence in Reliable AI (relAI) – MSc scholarship (TUM / LMU Munich)
host: relAI (DAAD-funded Konrad Zuse School), TU Munich & LMU Munich
coverage: Monthly scholarship for the remaining standard study period of the MSc, plus relAI training programme (modules, retreats, mentoring). TUM charges non-EU tuition, so check whether the stipend covers it.
amount: Monthly stipend. The amount was not captured on the official page; one third-party listing cites €934/month (unverified).
fields: MSc programmes in CS, mathematics, engineering, natural sciences, data science/ML/AI at TUM or LMU; topic must relate to reliable AI (safety, security, privacy, responsibility)
eligibility: Excellent bachelor's in CS/math/engineering/related field. Must be (or become) enrolled in an eligible MSc at TUM or LMU; offers are conditional on admission. Two referees, a supervisor preference and a motivation statement are required.
english: C1 or equivalent. The official page also accepts 'proof that University degree was taught mainly in English', so an MOI letter from FAST should work. Note that TUM/LMU admission itself may have its own English rules.
deadline: The 2026 MSc call is closed. The next call (for an Oct 2027 start) is not yet announced. One third-party site lists 22 Nov 2026 (unverified). Apply to the TUM/LMU MSc in parallel; most of those deadlines are end of May.
fitReason: This is the best AI-specific funding found that explicitly accepts an English-taught degree instead of IELTS, and his LLM/RAG and medical-imaging work fits the reliable-AI topics. It is very competitive with a 3.41 CGPA, and TUM tuition for non-EU students adds cost.
steps: Watch zuseschoolrelai.de/application from Nov 2026 for the 2027 MSc call
Pick 1–3 relAI faculty as preferred supervisors and draft a reliable-AI topic (e.g. trustworthy RAG / medical imaging robustness)
Get the FAST MOI letter plus HEC-attested transcripts/degree
Line up two referees (FAST FYP supervisor + Imperium Dynamics manager)
Submit the relAI application online with CV, transcripts, motivation, supervisor choices and English proof
Separately apply to an eligible TUM or LMU MSc (Informatics / Data Engineering & Analytics / Data Science) by its deadline (often 31 May)
If selected, accept the relAI offer conditional on MSc admission

name: ELIZA (Konrad Zuse School of Excellence in Learning and Intelligent Systems) – Master's scholarship
host: ELIZA / DAAD, partner universities incl. TU Darmstadt, Uni Freiburg, Saarland, TU Berlin, Heidelberg, Tübingen and others
coverage: Monthly stipend at DAAD rates during the master's, plus ELIZA network events. Cannot be combined with other scholarships.
fields: Machine learning / AI master's at ELIZA partner sites (e.g. TU Darmstadt CS/AI)
eligibility: Excellent students in (or admitted to) a CS/AI master's at an ELIZA site. Must comply with DAAD stipend rules.
english: Follows the host master's programme's rules. Not verified whether an MOI letter is accepted.
deadline: Reported cut-off dates are 25 April and 25 October each year (university news source, unverified). For an Oct 2027 start, the 25 April 2027 cut-off is the target, assuming you hold an admission by then.
fitReason: This is a strong AI-specific option if he is admitted to TU Darmstadt or another ELIZA site. It is highly selective, the official page could not be read (JS-rendered), and the details are unverified.
steps: Apply to an ELIZA partner master's (TU Darmstadt MSc Computer Science / AI-related) for winter 2027
Check eliza.school (Master's track) for the current call and the cut-off (expected 25 Apr 2027)
Prepare CV, transcripts, motivation letter on ML interests, referee contacts and an ELIZA supervisor preference
Submit the online application before the cut-off; interviews follow for shortlisted candidates

name: HPI scholarship for international Computer Science (M.Sc.) students
host: Hasso Plattner Institute (Digital Engineering Faculty, Uni Potsdam)
coverage: Monthly stipend for the standard 4 semesters
fields: HPI M.Sc. Computer Science (check whether Data Engineering / Digital Health are included in the next call)
eligibility: Excellently qualified foreign nationals or stateless graduates whose first degree was not obtained in Germany. Degree must be completed by the scholarship start. Awarded only if you get and accept a full-time place for that intake.
english: HPI master's admission rules apply. Not verified whether an MOI letter is accepted.
deadline: Past calls (2024): 12 May 2024 for winter 2024/25 and 8 Nov 2024 for summer 2025. The current HPI scholarship page lists only bachelor's scholarships, so no 2027 master's call is confirmed.
fitReason: €1,100/month for 2 years would nearly cover living costs in Potsdam, and the programme is English and AI/systems-heavy. The call may not recur, so ask master-info@hpi.de.
steps: Email master-info@hpi.de asking whether the international M.Sc. scholarship runs for winter 2027/28
Apply to the HPI M.Sc. (Computer Science / Data Engineering) via the HPI/Uni Potsdam portal by its deadline
If a call opens (historically ~April–May for the winter intake), submit the scholarship application with CV, transcripts and motivation
Accept the study place to activate the scholarship

name: 28DIGITAL (formerly EIT Digital) Master School scholarships
host: 28DIGITAL Education Foundation (EIT Digital), with partner universities (e.g. Aalto, KTH, TU Berlin, ELTE, BME, Turku, Twente and others)
coverage: For all students: merit-based full or half tuition-fee waivers for 2 years. 'Scholarships of Excellence' (full waiver + living allowance) under EU projects are for EU/EEA citizens only. Some partner-university awards are open to non-EU students (e.g. ELTE up to €10,000/yr + €1,000 travel; BME up to €3,500/semester).
amount: Full or half tuition waiver. Non-EU tuition is roughly €18,000/yr (unverified). No living allowance for non-EU students from 28DIGITAL itself.
fields: Data Science, AI with Affective Computing, Autonomous Systems, Cloud/HPC, Cyber Security, FinTech, HCI/XR, Intelligent Chips and Systems
eligibility: Relevant bachelor's. Two-year programme across an entry university and an exit university, plus an Innovation & Entrepreneurship minor. €75 application fee. A €500 deposit is required to secure awards of ≥50%.
english: University-specific tests. An MOI letter is generally NOT enough: e.g. Aalto needs TOEFL 92 / IELTS 6.5 and states that a university statement or proficiency letter is not sufficient. Exemptions exist only for degrees from listed countries (Pakistan is not listed).
deadline: 2027/28 intake: Period 1 (for non-EU students needing a visa) runs 30 Oct 2026 – 31 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET
fitReason: The AI/data tracks fit him well and the deadline is near. A tuition waiver alone does not cover living costs for two countries, and it effectively requires IELTS/TOEFL. Worth applying only for a full waiver plus a cheap entry country (e.g. Hungary/ELTE).
steps: Portal opens 30 Oct 2026: create an account at masterschool.eitdigital.eu
Choose a programme (e.g. Data Science or AI) and the entry/exit university pair
Book IELTS/TOEFL early unless the chosen entry university explicitly exempts you
Prepare CV, transcripts, degree, a 2-page motivation letter with an entrepreneurial idea, and English proof
In tab 4 of the portal, tick the 28DIGITAL scholarship and any partner-university scholarships (e.g. ELTE/BME)
Submit and pay the €75 fee by 31 Jan 2027
If awarded ≥50%, pay the €250 registration fee + €500 deposit within 7 days

name: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines
coverage: Monthly stipend, insurance, travel allowance, annual study allowance, possible rent subsidy
fields: All (except art/architecture, which have separate programmes)
eligibility: Degree no more than 6 years old. Resident in Germany for no more than 15 months. Funding must begin in 2027 (usually 1 Oct 2027). Offered only for certain countries: NOT listed on the DAAD Pakistan programme page, and the portal showed 'currently you cannot apply' for the country filter tested.
english: Certificates such as IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Duolingo or Cambridge. An MOI letter is not listed as acceptable for the DAAD application.
deadline: Not offered to Pakistani applicants (the window usually opens 1 June; deadlines vary by country, e.g. 17 Nov 2025 for Poland)
fitReason: This is the classic DAAD master's scholarship, but DAAD Pakistan does not list it for Pakistan. Pakistani graduates are routed to EPOS / Helmut-Schmidt instead.
steps: Confirm with DAAD Islamabad (daad.pk) whether Pakistan is eligible for the 2027 call; if not, skip

name: DAAD EPOS – Development-Related Postgraduate Courses 2027/28
coverage: Full scholarship: monthly stipend, insurance, travel; tuition covered or waived on most courses
fields: The official 2027/28 course list has no CS/AI/data-science course. The closest is MSc Photogrammetry and Geoinformatics (HfT Stuttgart). Others cover development economics, energy, water, urban planning, health and forestry.
eligibility: Applicants from developing countries, including Pakistan. Bachelor's plus usually ≥2 years of relevant professional experience after graduation. Degree no more than 6 years old.
english: Course-specific. Usually IELTS/TOEFL; some courses accept MOI (check each course).
deadline: 2027/28 intake: each course sets its own deadline ('see website of the course'), typically Aug–Dec 2026 or into Jan 2027
bond: None found formally, but applicants must show a development motivation and are expected to contribute to home-country development
fitReason: There is no CS/AI course, and an AI-engineering profile does not match development-sector courses. He may also fall short of 2 years of post-graduation experience. Only geoinformatics is a stretch.
steps: Read the 2027/28 EPOS course list (official PDF) and pick a course (e.g. HfT Stuttgart Photogrammetry & Geoinformatics)
Check that course's own deadline and documents on its website
Apply directly to the course (not to DAAD), including the DAAD application form, CV (Europass), motivation letter, employer certificate and references
The course pre-selects candidates and forwards them to DAAD for the final decision

name: DAAD Helmut-Schmidt-Programme – Master's in Public Policy and Good Governance
coverage: Full scholarship: stipend, tuition, insurance, travel, German course
fields: Public policy, governance, economics, law, political science (8 partner universities). No CS/AI.
eligibility: Graduates from listed countries, including Pakistan. Relevant degree and social/political engagement.
deadline: Generally end of July (DAAD Pakistan). The 2026 window (1 Jun–31 Jul 2026, third-party report) was for the Oct 2027 start and is now closed.
fitReason: This is a policy degree, not CS/AI, and the window for a 2027 start has passed.
steps: Skip unless switching to an AI-policy career; the next window is ~June–July 2027 for a 2028 start

name: Deutschlandstipendium – TU Darmstadt
host: TU Darmstadt with private sponsors and the federal government
coverage: Monthly stipend, merit-based, independent of income and nationality
fields: All
eligibility: All TU Darmstadt students, including first-semester students. Master's students must be no higher than the 2nd subject semester at application. First-semester students are ranked by the grade of their qualifying degree.
deadline: Last cycle: 21 Sep – 18 Oct 2026. For an Oct 2027 start, expect ~late Sep – mid Oct 2027, right after enrolment.
fitReason: The application falls after arrival, so he can apply as a new master's student; €300/month eases the budget. A 3.41 CGPA converts to a mid German grade, which makes it competitive but possible.
steps: Enrol at TU Darmstadt for winter 2027/28
In the window (~Sep–Oct 2027), fill in the online form on the TU Darmstadt Deutschlandstipendium portal (phase 1)
If shortlisted, upload documents to the department within the stated deadline (1–2 weeks): CV, motivation, transcripts, evidence of engagement
Contact: dls-bewerbung@tu-darmstadt.de

name: Deutschlandstipendium – TU Dortmund
fields: All
eligibility: First-year students and current bachelor's/master's students of all nationalities. For first-semester master's funding, enrolment must be in place by the start of winter semester at the latest (faculty notes).
deadline: Last cycle: 15 Aug – 15 Sep 2026. For 2027, expect ~15 Aug – 15 Sep 2027, i.e. before arrival, so apply as an admitted student.
fitReason: Incoming students can apply before the semester, so he could secure funding for year 1 at Dortmund.
steps: Obtain the TU Dortmund admission (e.g. MSc Data Science / Computer Science)
Apply online during 15 Aug – 15 Sep 2027 via the TU Dortmund Deutschlandstipendium portal
Upload CV, transcripts, motivation and engagement evidence; complete enrolment by the semester start

name: Deutschlandstipendium – University of Göttingen
fields: All
eligibility: Students starting at Göttingen in the winter semester can apply after enrolling
deadline: Last cycle: 1–30 Sep 2026. Expect ~1–30 Sep 2027.
fitReason: Usable in his first semester if he enrols in an English CS/Applied Data Science master's at Göttingen.
steps: Enrol at Göttingen (enrolment usually opens Aug/Sep)
Apply online in September 2027 via the university's Deutschlandstipendium page
Submit CV, motivation letter, bachelor's transcript and evidence of engagement

name: Deutschlandstipendium (and Lore-Auerbach scholarship) – University of Hildesheim
fields: All (Hildesheim offers an English MSc in Data Analytics)
eligibility: Hildesheim students; whether admitted but not yet enrolled students may apply is not verified
deadline: Usually in June (2026 cycle: 1–30 June 2026). Expect June 2027, before arrival.
fitReason: The June window comes before an Oct 2027 start, so he must ask whether admitted applicants qualify; otherwise he can apply in June 2028 for year 2.
steps: Email stipend@uni-hildesheim.de asking whether admitted first-semester master's students can apply in June 2027
If yes, apply online in June 2027 with CV, motivation and transcripts
Otherwise apply in June 2028 for the second year

name: Deutschlandstipendium – University of Würzburg
fields: All
eligibility: Students and first-year students (incoming students may apply)
deadline: Last cycle deadline: 16 July 2026. Expect mid-July 2027.
fitReason: First-year students can apply, so he can apply in July 2027 once admitted to an English master's at Würzburg.
steps: Get admitted to a Würzburg master's for WS 2027/28
Apply online by mid-July 2027 via the Würzburg Deutschlandstipendium portal
Upload CV, transcripts, motivation letter and engagement evidence

name: Deutschlandstipendium – University of Passau
fields: All (Passau: MSc AI Engineering, Computer Science)
eligibility: Students and prospective students (eligibility of admitted-but-not-enrolled internationals not verified)
deadline: 2026 cycle: 4 May – 15 June 2026. Applications reopen in May 2027.
fitReason: The window falls before arrival and Passau admission decisions may come later, so the timing is tight. Apply for year 2 if he misses it.
steps: Apply early for Passau master's admission (winter 2027/28)
In May–June 2027, submit the online form (reactivated when the 2027 period opens)
Upload documents as instructed; results come before the 1 Oct funding start

name: Deutschlandstipendium (Universitätsstipendium) – University of Potsdam (incl. HPI Digital Engineering)
fields: All faculties. HPI master's students are enrolled at Uni Potsdam's Digital Engineering Faculty (HPI-specific eligibility not confirmed).
eligibility: Students and prospective students. First-semester master's students are ranked by their bachelor's final grade.
deadline: Every year from 1 July for 3 weeks (2025: 1–22 July). Expect ~1–22 July 2027.
fitReason: Prospective students may apply explicitly, so he can apply in July 2027 after an HPI/Potsdam admission.
steps: Get admitted to the HPI M.Sc. or another Potsdam master's
Apply online during 1–~22 July 2027 on the Uni Potsdam Universitätsstipendium portal (no paper)
Provide CV, motivation, bachelor's transcript/final grade and engagement evidence

name: Deutschlandstipendium – Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences
fields: All
eligibility: Students of all nationalities and disciplines enrolled at Frankfurt UAS (first-year students within the standard study period are supported)
deadline: 2026 cycle: 1–20 May 2026. The 2027 window will be published in March/April 2027.
fitReason: The May window requires enrolment, so a new Oct 2027 student realistically applies in May 2028 for year 2 only.
steps: Enrol at Frankfurt UAS (e.g. MSc High Integrity Systems)
Check the page in Mar/Apr 2028 and apply in the May portal window with a 1–1.5-page motivation letter and evidence

name: STIBET / university grants for international students (completion grants, TU Darmstadt and others)
host: DAAD STIBET funds administered by each university's International Office
coverage: Short-term stipends, mostly for the final (thesis) phase or emergencies; some universities also run merit awards for internationals
amount: Typically a few hundred € per month for a few months (varies by university, unverified)
fields: All
eligibility: International students already enrolled, usually in the final semesters with good progress; some require social engagement
deadline: Set by each university, usually once or twice per semester. Only relevant from ~2028 onward.
fitReason: This is only a top-up for the thesis phase, not entry funding, but useful as a safety net later.
steps: After enrolment, check the International Office scholarship page (e.g. TU Darmstadt 'STIBET Abschlussstipendium')
Apply during the final 1–2 semesters with transcript, supervisor letter and finance plan

name: Heinrich Böll Foundation – scholarship for international graduate students
fields: All, at state-recognised German universities; master's must be ≥4 semesters
eligibility: International students with a first degree from abroad can apply before starting the master's in Germany. Priority for DAC-country applicants not yet resident in Germany. Requires very good grades plus demonstrable social/political (green) engagement.
english: German B2 / DSH required per the FAQ. English and MOI are not sufficient.
deadline: 15 Jan – 1 Mar 2027 (spring) or 15 Jul – 1 Sep 2027 (autumn). The official page warns that from 1 Mar 2027 only 'first-cycle programs' will be accepted; confirm with studienwerk@boell.de.
fitReason: This is the one foundation open to applicants still abroad, but it needs German B2 and strong activism, and the 2027 rule change may exclude master's applicants.
steps: Email studienwerk@boell.de to confirm master's eligibility after the 1 Mar 2027 change
Obtain German B2 if pursuing it
Submit the online application (15 Jan – 1 Mar 2027) with CV, motivation essay on engagement, transcripts, admission/application proof and a professor's reference
Attend the selection interview if shortlisted

name: Konrad Adenauer Foundation – Ausländerförderung (non-EU graduates)
fields: All
eligibility: Non-EU applicants with a completed degree who want a master's (≥4 semesters remaining) at a German university. Requires a Christian-democratic value orientation and engagement.
english: German language skills required (Goethe-Uni overview). MOI is not sufficient.
deadline: Once a year: 15 July (Ausländerförderung). 15 July 2027 would suit a WS 2027/28 start only if he already has admission.
fitReason: It needs German and political/social engagement aligned with KAS values, which conflicts with his English-only preference.
steps: Learn German to at least B1/B2
Apply online by 15 July with CV, essay, transcripts, admission letter and 2 references
Attend the selection meeting

name: Friedrich Ebert (FES), Friedrich Naumann (FNF) and Rosa Luxemburg (RLS) foundations – international student programmes
fields: All
eligibility: Non-EU programmes exist. FES and RLS fund international students already studying at a German university. FNF funds international master's students at German universities (minimum 2 semesters of funding). All require political engagement in line with the foundation.
english: German skills required (FES, RLS 'very good German'). Not verified for FNF. MOI is not sufficient.
deadline: Not verified for 2027. Most accept applications only once enrolled in Germany, so the earliest is during the first semester (2027/28).
fitReason: They require enrolment in Germany plus German language and political engagement, so they are useful only as a second-year option if he learns German.
steps: After enrolment, check fes.de/studienfoerderung, freiheit.org/begabtenfoerderung and rosalux.de for international-programme deadlines
Prepare German certificate, CV, political-engagement essay and references

name: Hans Böckler, Hanns Seidel and Avicenna-Studienwerk (Muslim) – not open to non-EU applicants from abroad
fields: All
eligibility: Limited to EU citizens and §8 BAföG-eligible residents (Bildungsinländer). A Pakistani newcomer does not qualify.
deadline: Not applicable
fitReason: He is ineligible as a non-EU national without §8 BAföG status. Listed only so he doesn't waste time on these.
steps: Skip

name: KAAD (Catholic Academic Exchange Service) scholarship
fields: All
eligibility: Students from developing/emerging countries. Catholic affiliation or motivation for interreligious dialogue. No direct applications: nomination by a Catholic university parish (KHG) in Germany or a KAAD partner committee abroad.
deadline: Set by partner committees. Not verified.
bond: Return expected: KAAD targets applicants who intend to return home after their studies (conflicts with the earn-abroad plan)
fitReason: It is church-nominated and return-oriented, which suits neither his profile nor his plan to work abroad first.
steps: Skip unless connected to a Catholic partner institution in Pakistan

name: Company and research-institute funding (Bayer Foundation, Siemens, Max Planck / Helmholtz schools)
host: Bayer Foundation, Siemens, Max Planck / Helmholtz
coverage: Varies; mostly not full master's funding
fields: STEM
eligibility: Bayer Foundation fellowships mainly fund German/EU students going abroad or specific life-science projects. Max Planck (IMPRS) and Helmholtz schools fund PhDs, not master's. Siemens has no general open master's scholarship for Pakistanis (not verified). A paid HiWi job or working student role is the realistic route.
deadline: Not applicable
fitReason: No verified full master's scholarship found here. Instead, target working-student jobs (20 h/week) at AI firms and HiWi posts at Max Planck/Helmholtz/DFKI once enrolled.
steps: After arrival, apply for HiWi / working student roles at DFKI, Max Planck, Helmholtz and companies
